leaks_ranked.step: In-app OCCASION screen: role picked -> reached the create/message screen (#buyerSection/#receiverSection -> Page - Create Viewed)
leaks_ranked.why_real: Person-linked in PostHog (safe, not a count ratio) and STABLE across both windows: ~23-25% of role-committed users never reach the create screen. Grounded in a concrete structural flaw -- the dominant tap target on this screen (the example video card, handleExampleClick) only PLAYS the video (a dead-end); forward progress hides in a small per-card '📝 Customize Template' button and a 'Create from Scratch' button below an 'or' separator. Loss of 13 and 12 people -- the larger half of the role->Create leak, and it has NEVER been attacked.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: ~13 role-committed users/fortnight who never reach Create. Each recovered one is worth ~0.86 (reached->press) x 1.0 (press->start, 100% this window) x ~0.30 (start->review) ~= 0.26 reviews -- the funnel's highest per-head review yield, because these users already survived every earlier gate. Full recovery ceiling ~3-4 reviews/fortnight (unmeasurable, but the highest-value slice).

leaks_ranked.step: In-app CREATE screen: reached create screen -> pressed Create Video (Page - Create Viewed -> Create Video Button Clicked)
leaks_ranked.why_real: A genuine but SMALLER and noisier drop: only 6 people lost this window (9 prior). The recommended brainstorm angle (sticky Create button) targets exactly this sub-step, but the evidence shows it is already at 86% this window -- the create button is NOT where the big loss sits. Runner-up, not the pick.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: ~6-9 users/fortnight. Same ~0.28 reviews/recovered-user value, but roughly half the headcount of the occasion-screen drop and already converting at 86%, so a lower ceiling.

leaks_ranked.step: Claim page email gate: landed -> gave email
leaks_ranked.why_real: The largest single drop by raw headcount (~80/fortnight never submit) and flat across windows (+1.6pts, p=0.785, NOT SIGNIFICANT). Real, but its dominant cause is known first-paint non-engagement, it was attacked with 3 distinct mechanisms (PR #8 + two 2026-07-23 ships, both pending), and it feeds reviews weakly per head (many one-off gift buyers who never place the 'next order' the discount rewards).
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: High raw headcount but low review-value-per-head and freshly worked; deprioritised this cycle.

biggest_leak: The in-app OCCASION screen (role picked -> reached the create screen) -- the larger, stabler, never-touched half of the role->Create leak the brainstorm chose, sitting inside the highest per-head review engine in the funnel.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: Reviews arrive ~100% from the in-app thank-you screen (measured: 10/10 this window, 7/8 prior; 0 from email_redirect in both), which appears only after a finished video. Pressing Create -> video_started is ~93-100% and video_started -> review ~30%, so every role-committed user recovered to reach+press Create is worth ~0.26 reviews. The occasion-screen drop is ~13 such users/fortnight vs ~6 for the create-screen button drop, so it has the higher total expected value inside the same review engine.
choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: The coverage map records the occasion/examples screen as ZERO prior attempts ('never attacked'). The only prior work on the wider role->Create leak is the 2026-07-06 message-box default pre-fill + NAME fix, a DIFFERENT screen (#createSection) that fences only that mechanism. Fresh ground.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all past changes: adding/surfacing a NEW element that answers a real motivation moved the funnel (2026-06-16 value-prop hero + email-first = the only measured win); generic reshuffles did nothing (PR #8 = flat). This change follows the winning pattern -- it fixes a concrete affordance (make the obvious tap target advance) rather than restyling for taste -- while staying honest that at ~56 role-pickers/fortnight it sits inside the noise floor.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: The recommended sticky-Create-button angle targets the create-screen sub-step, already 86% (only 6 lost) -- smaller, noisier, lower ceiling. The claim email gate is bigger by headcount but flat, thrice-attacked, freshly worked, and feeds reviews weakly per head. Preview/share review asks (~0 clicks) are a known dead surface. Arrived->role was shipped against on 2026-08-01 and is freshly fenced.

diagnosis.question: Within the role->Create leak the brainstorm chose, WHERE does the loss fall -- on the occasion screen (never reaching Create) or on the create screen (reaching it but not pressing the button)? And WHY do role-committed users stall on the occasion screen?
hypotheses_considered: Create button below the fold / not sticky, so ready users can't reach it (the recommended angle's cause)
Occasion-screen affordance confusion: the dominant tap target (the example video) is a dead-end that only plays; the forward actions are small/secondary and partly below an 'or'
Extra-hop fatigue: the occasion screen is a redundant transition before the message screen
Genuine drop-off / lost interest after committing to a role (a ceiling no layout moves)
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Built a person-linked PostHog sub-funnel splitting role->Create into role->Page-Create-Viewed and Page-Create-Viewed->Create-Clicked, for both frozen windows (autocapture 'Page - Create Viewed' / 'Create Video Button Clicked' / 'User Selected ...'). Read the occasion-screen markup (#buyerSection/#receiverSection, lines 1034-1145) and handleExampleClick (line 2054), plus the create-screen markup (#createSection, #products carousel, #generateBtn line 1286). Pulled the recent session_recordings list (4 index.html recordings in-window, most idle) and reconstructed the event timeline of the engaged in-app sessions.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The loss splits two ways and the OCCASION screen is the larger, stabler half: role->reached-create is 77% (43/56) this window and 75% (36/48) prior -- ~13 and ~12 lost; reached-create->pressed is 86% (37/43) this window vs 75% (27/36) prior -- only 6 and 9 lost. The occasion screen has a code-verified affordance flaw (video-card tap is a dead-end; forward action secondary) and has never been attacked. This CONTRADICTS the recommended angle's premise that the create button is the big loss (already 86%). The one reconstructable engaged in-app replay (session 019ff38c) went role -> 'Create from Scratch' -> Create-Viewed -> pressed Create within 4s -- no button-hunt.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: At ~56 role-pickers/fortnight neither sub-step's window-over-window move is significant, and the 77% vs 86% split is itself within noise -- I rank by the LEVEL + stability + the never-touched structural flaw, not a proven delta. The instruments are blind to WHY someone leaves the occasion screen: no scroll-depth, video-play-duration, or button-focus events between role-select and Create-Viewed, and only ~4 index.html recordings in-window (most idle), so I cannot directly confirm 'tapped the video, watched, didn't see the forward button' vs 'lost interest'. The affordance flaw is real in the code; that it causes the 23% drop is a well-grounded bet, not a proven fact.

plan.title: Make the occasion screen advance: turn the example card into the primary forward action, keep preview, quiet the fork
plan.targets: In-app occasion/examples screen -- role picked -> reached the create/message screen (#buyerSection / #receiverSection)
plan.mechanism: Today the biggest, most obvious tap target on the occasion screen -- the example video card -- is a dead-end: handleExampleClick only plays/pauses the video. The two ways FORWARD are visually secondary: a small '📝 Customize Template' button pinned on each card, and a 'Create from Scratch' primary button hidden below an 'or' separator. A role-committed user who taps the card to see what this is watches a video and lands back where they started, with no clear next step. This change flips the hierarchy so the obvious action is the forward one: (1) tapping the example card body now ADVANCES to the message screen with that template pre-filled (via useTemplate's existing path), instead of playing; (2) each card keeps an explicit, visible play/preview control so the example video is still watchable on demand (the payoff is not lost); (3) each card gets a clear primary 'Use this ->' affordance in place of the muted '📝 Customize Template' label; (4) 'Create from Scratch' is kept but demoted to a calm secondary text link ('or write your own') so there is ONE clear primary path and one quiet alternative. No step, gate, reward, role, or template is removed.
plan.assumed_cause: Occasion-screen affordance confusion: the dominant tap target (the example video) does not advance the flow, and the real forward actions are small/secondary and partly below an 'or', so ~23-25% of role-committed users stall on this screen and never reach Create.

cause_verification.for: Person-linked PostHog sub-funnel (both frozen windows): role->reached-create-screen is 77% (43/56) this window and 75% (36/48) prior -- a stable ~23-25% loss BEFORE the create screen, i.e. on the occasion screen. The markup confirms the flaw directly: handleExampleClick (index.html:2054) only calls toggleExamplePlay -- the card tap plays the video and does nothing else; forward progress lives in the per-card '📝 Customize Template' button (1057/1070/1083...) and the 'Create from Scratch' button below an 'or' paragraph (1086-1088). The most tempting tap is a dead-end and the forward path is secondary.
cause_verification.against: I actively searched for evidence that the loss is NOT on the occasion screen. Two checks could have contradicted the cause: (a) the reached-create->pressed sub-step -- if THAT were the dominant drop, the loss would be at the button, not the occasion screen; it is 86% (37/43) this window, only 6 lost, so the button is NOT the big loss -- my cause survives. (b) Session replays -- I reconstructed the event timeline of the engaged in-app recordings; the one that reached the create screen (session 019ff38c) pressed Create within 4s of arriving, no button-hunt, again pointing away from the button cause. What I could NOT do: directly watch someone tap the video, watch it, and abandon the occasion screen -- only ~4 index.html recordings exist in-window and most are idle, with no scroll/play-duration events. So I cannot rule out that some of the 23% are a genuine interest ceiling rather than affordance confusion.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The location of the loss is measured, person-linked, and stable across both windows: it falls MORE on the occasion screen (13/56) than on the create button (6/43), and the occasion screen has a concrete, code-verified affordance flaw plus zero prior attempts. Even under the honest limit that some of the 23% may be a ceiling no layout moves, making the obvious tap target advance (while preserving preview and the from-scratch path) is a low-risk, fully reversible presentation change with the highest per-head review value in the funnel -- exactly the small compounding bet this job exists to make. It does not remove the reason anyone is here (the exchange is untouched), so the downside is bounded.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Users who convert here are ready to make the video and manage to find the forward action; they get a fast path to a pre-filled, on-brand message they can send in one more tap. The occasion screen asks nothing in exchange -- it is not a gate, it is a routing screen whose only job is to pick which template pre-fills the box. So the rate is not a price being accepted; it is pure navigation efficiency, which is why an affordance fix (not a motivation or exchange change) is the right lever: there is no reward being withheld to protect.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the 23% who stall on the occasion screen do so because the forward action is unclear (not purely because they lost interest).
Making the card tap advance does not frustrate users who wanted to preview -- mitigated by keeping an explicit visible play control and the Back button.

Landing on the message screen with a pre-filled template (rather than an autoplay video) is not a downgrade in perceived payoff -- the pre-filled message and the retained preview keep the value visible.
The template pre-fill and swapNamePlaceholder path (already used by useTemplate/applyPendingTemplate) works when triggered from a card-body tap.
plan.second_order_effects: Advancing on card tap will shift the mix from 'Create from Scratch' toward template-based entries (template_used up, from-scratch down) -- harmless; templates are on-brand starting points. Some users who currently tap to preview will now advance instead; if they only wanted to watch, they can still tap the explicit play control or press Back -- and advancing is not a commitment (no video is generated until they press Create on the next screen, 86% likely once there). Downstream: this touches only the in-app occasion screen; email capture (claim page, upstream), the discount code, and video-by-email delivery are all untouched, and reviews via email_redirect are 0 in both windows -- so no review-reminder cost. The only review path this feeds is the in-app thank-you screen, which this change helps by getting more role-committed users to a finished video.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the 77% vs 86% split is within noise (13 vs 6 people), the brainstorm picked the create button for a reason, and you are second-guessing the slate on a coin-flip; worse, making the card advance REMOVES the pre-commit video preview that is the only place users feel the payoff (brainstorm angle #4's thesis), so you might depress motivation and lose more than you gain. My answer: I am not ranking on the WoW delta -- I rank on the LEVEL (the occasion-screen drop is the larger half in BOTH windows, 13 and 12 vs 6 and 9) combined with never-touched status and a concrete code-verified affordance flaw, which the create button (already 86%, one engaged replay pressed it in 4s) does not have. And I explicitly PRESERVE the preview: every card keeps a visible play control, so the payoff stays one tap away -- it demotes the video from 'accidental dead-end' to 'deliberate preview', which is strictly clearer, not a removal. If it re-measures flat, the honest read is 'affordance was not the binding constraint / interest ceiling', not a claimed win -- the entry ships labelled unmeasurable-by-design.
plan.expected_effect: A few more role-committed users per fortnight reach the create screen (and, at 86% press-through, a finished video and the in-app review ask). Small in absolute terms and below the noise floor; valuable because it is the highest per-head review slice and compounds.

tradeoff.gained: More role-committed users find the forward action and reach Create -> finished video -> the in-app thank-you review ask (the only surface producing reviews -- 10/10 this window). Highest per-head review value in the funnel.
tradeoff.risked: The pre-commit example video becomes a deliberate tap (via the play control) rather than the default card action, so some passive previewing is lost; if any of the 23% were a genuine interest ceiling, they will not be recovered. No measurable downstream cost: review clicks via email_redirect (Klaviyo reminders) are 0 in both windows (this: 10/10 in_app; prior: 7/8 in_app + 1 share), and email capture / code / video delivery are all upstream and untouched.

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: The occasion/examples screen has NEVER been attacked (coverage map). Not the 2026-07-06 message-step fix (that changed the textarea DEFAULT and removed the NAME alert on a DIFFERENT screen, #createSection -- fences only that mechanism). Not PR #8 or either 2026-07-23 ship (all claim-page). Not the 2026-08-01 welcome re-rank (welcome screen, above role-pick, freshly fenced). It does NOT develop the recommended slate angle (sticky Create button) because the evidence shows the create-screen sub-step is already 86% -- the smaller half of the leak; it develops slate ANGLE #2 ('Rebuild the occasion screen around one obvious forward tap'), which the brainstorm itself flagged as the strongest alternative on a never-touched surface. No owner rejection touches this screen (both are claim-page/video-ready-screen review-ask rejections).
plan.how_to_verify: Build, then boot locally (PORT=3939 node server.js) and load index.html with a role pre-selected; confirm: tapping an example card body advances to #createSection with that template pre-filled (no NAME leftover); the explicit play control still plays/pauses the example video in place; 'Use this ->' reads as the primary card action; 'Create from Scratch' survives as a quiet secondary link and still routes to a defaulted message; Back still works. Render mobile BEFORE/AFTER PNGs under cycle-artifacts/2026-08-15/. Re-measure ~2026-08-29 with the person-linked PostHog sub-funnel (role events -> 'Page - Create Viewed' -> 'Create Video Button Clicked') on both frozen windows, then significance-test role->reached-create; never claim 'worked' without a SIGNIFICANT result. Create no Supabase test rows (screenshot loads only; intercept /api/track).
alternatives_rejected: Recommended slate angle #1 (sticky/docked Create button on #createSection): targets reached-create->pressed, already 86% (6 lost) this window -- the smaller, noisier half of the leak; lower ceiling. The character selector is also a horizontal carousel (one ~130px row), not the nine-tall vertical grid the brainstorm described, so the below-the-fold severity is overstated.

Slate angle #3 (collapse occasion into the message screen as inline chips): higher ceiling but a larger flow change that removes a screen -- closer to touching process; keep as a follow-up if angle #2 reads flat.

Slate angle #4 (finished-video preview at the commit point) and #6 (reassurance microcopy at the button): both address the create SCREEN, the smaller sub-step, and rest more on unproven motivation bets than on a measured location-of-loss.
Slate angle #5 (resolve character from SKU): a bigger logic change with a mismatch edge case, on the smaller create-screen sub-step.

Full 'whole card advances, drop all preview' rebuild: rejected because it would remove the pre-commit video preview entirely (angle #4's concern); this plan keeps preview via an explicit play control.
